label: HEALING

cover.headline: Stop replaying it: *quiet the “what ifs”*
cover.sub: 5 ways to step out of the loop.

points.heading: Notice the loop
points.body: Replaying it rarely brings new answers, just more hurt.
points.panel: “I’m replaying it again. I can pause.”

points.heading: Give it a time slot
points.body: Let yourself think it through for ten minutes, then stop.
points.panel: Set a ten-minute timer to journal, then close the book.

points.heading: Move your body
points.body: A walk or stretch can break a thought spiral.
points.panel: Take a ten-minute walk without your phone.

points.heading: Write the kinder story
points.body: Look back with compassion for who you were then.
points.panel: “I did my best with what I knew.”

points.heading: Talk it through once
points.body: Saying it out loud to someone safe can let it settle.
points.panel: “Can I vent for a few minutes? I keep going over it.”

close.save: Save this for the replay nights.

caption:
After a breakup, the mind loves to rewind: what if I’d said this, what if I hadn’t done that.

It’s a normal part of healing, but it can keep you stuck. These five gentle ways help you step out of the loop and back into your day. Healing isn’t a straight line, and that’s okay.
